- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.11) and recent prices are rising — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially <0.0) or recent sentiment is bearish — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +2–3% in 1–2 days) by forecasting higher prices for 30-day horizon — apply lag correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for spikes >1.5% in last 3 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 10–15 day average is >10% above recent 30d, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overbought bias.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.0–0.11), model often overestimates — apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0% to align with true mean.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to “late correction” — true values often dip after model peaks — adjust by reducing final 5–7 days of forecast by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is weak or negative.
